business_summary: Coca-Cola is a total-beverage company whose products are sold in more than 200 countries and territories at a rate of 2.2 billion servings per day. It is mostly NOT a manufacturer: its core 'concentrate operations' sell beverage concentrates, syrups and fountain syrups to a network of independent, authorized bottlers, who add water and sweetener, package, and distribute the finished drinks. Coca-Cola keeps the brands, the marketing and the recipe; the bottlers carry the factories, trucks and working capital. That structure makes KO unusually asset-light: FY2025 revenue of $47.941B was produced on only $2.112B of capital expenditure and $1.050B of depreciation & amortization, generating a 61.6% gross margin and a 28.7% operating margin. A smaller 'Bottling Investments' segment holds bottlers KO has taken back temporarily before refranchising them (the pending sale of Coca-Cola Beverages Africa is the current example, carried as $5.342B of assets held for sale at 2025-12-31). The Coca-Cola system sold 33.8 billion unit cases in 2025 vs 33.7 billion in 2024; sparkling soft drinks were 69% of worldwide unit case volume and Trademark Coca-Cola alone was 47%. Growth therefore comes mostly from price/mix and marketing, not from large volume gains — though Q2 2026 was a notable exception with unit case volume +5% and organic revenue +6%. James Quincey handed the CEO role to Henrique Braun on 2026-03-31 and became Executive Chairman.

moat.type: Global brand power + unmatched distribution/bottler network + scale in marketing and shelf space; asset-light concentrate royalty model with pricing power

quality.revenue_growth_3y: +3.7% CAGR FY2022 $43.004B -> FY2025 $47.941B; +7.8% CAGR over 5y from FY2020 $33.014B. Reported growth is depressed by currency; FY2026 guidance is ~5% organic growth and H1 2026 reported revenue was +9.2% ($25.852B vs $23.664B)
quality.roic: ~17.7% FY2025 (own calculation: NOPAT $11.301B = EBIT $13.762B x (1 - effective tax rate 17.88%, being tax $2.861B / pre-tax $15.998B); invested capital $63.961B = total equity $34.275B + total debt $45.492B - cash/ST investments/marketable securities $15.806B). Understated in spirit because ~$20.235B of equity-method bottler investments sit in invested capital while their profit shows up below the operating-income line as equity income, not in EBIT
quality.net_debt_to_ebitda: 2.00x at FY2025 year-end (net debt $29.686B / EBITDA $14.812B = EBIT $13.762B + D&A $1.050B); 1.71x at 2026-07-03 (net debt $27.172B / TTM EBITDA $15.888B). Gross debt is higher at $43.543B, so this depends on counting $16.371B of cash and securities as available
quality.fcf_positive: yes, but read the footnote. FY2025 GAAP free cash flow was only $5.296B (operating cash flow $7.408B - capex $2.112B) because KO paid $6.1B of the $6.2B final fairlife milestone in Q1 2025. KO's own non-GAAP 'free cash flow excluding the fairlife contingent consideration payment' was $11.4B. FY2024 was similarly depressed by a $6.0B IRS tax litigation deposit. H1 2026 operating cash flow was $7.5B and free cash flow $6.9B; FY2026 guidance is ~$12.4B FCF (~$14.6B operating cash flow less ~$2.2B capex)

valuation.method: Blend of two methods via code/valuation.py. (1) P/E: TTM diluted GAAP EPS $3.33 (FY2025 $3.04 - H1 2025 $1.65 + H1 2026 $1.94) x multiples 20 / 24 / 27 -> $66.60 / $79.92 / $89.91. (2) FCF yield: FY2025 free cash flow excluding the one-off fairlife payment $11.4B / 4,313M diluted shares = $2.643 per share, capitalised at 4.2% / 3.6% / 3.1% -> $62.93 / $73.42 / $85.26. Multiples are our own assumptions, not cited facts: 24x base is what we think a wide-moat staples compounder growing mid-single-digit organic revenue and high-single-digit EPS is worth; 20x low reflects a de-rating if volumes stall or the IRS case is lost; 27x high reflects continued 5%+ organic growth. SENSITIVITY: substituting FY2026 guided FCF of $12.4B ($2.875/share) raises the band to $67.53 / $79.89 / $91.33 and the base is still below today's price.
valuation.valuation_notes: At $88.01 KO trades at 26.4x TTM GAAP EPS of $3.33, ~26.7x the midpoint of FY2026 guided comparable EPS (FY2025 comparable EPS $3.00 grown 9-10% = $3.27-$3.30), a 3.0% FCF yield on FY2025 ex-fairlife FCF (3.3% on FY2026 guidance), and a 2.41% dividend yield on the 2026 annualised dividend of $2.12. Price is above our base fair value and essentially at the top of our band.

margin_of_safety_note: -0.1288 = (fair_value_base 76.67 - price 88.01) / price 88.01, the formula requested for this thesis. Note code/valuation.py and code/thesis.py use (base - price) / base, which gives -0.1479 for the same inputs. Either way the price is ABOVE fair value and there is NO margin of safety today. With state/config.json min_margin_of_safety = 0.12 (the code's convention), the buy trigger is roughly $67.50 or below.
conviction_note: Conviction 4 reflects business quality and the fact that every key number here is filing-backed. It is NOT a buy signal at $88.01: the price sits ~13% above our base fair value, so this is a watch-and-wait name pending a better entry.
bull_case: Wide, genuinely durable moat: 2.2 billion servings a day across 200+ countries, with Trademark Coca-Cola alone at 47% of worldwide unit case volume. Brand plus a bottler distribution network that cannot be replicated at any sensible cost.

Asset-light economics. FY2025 revenue of $47.941B needed only $2.112B of capex and $1.050B of D&A, producing a 61.6% gross margin and 28.7% operating margin. ROIC of ~17.7% (own calculation from FY2025 filing figures) compounds value.

Current operating momentum is real, not just price increases: Q2 2026 unit case volume grew 5%, organic revenue 6%, operating margin improved to 34.9% from 34.1%, and comparable EPS grew 11% to $0.97. KO raised FY2026 guidance on 2026-07-28 to ~5% organic revenue growth and 9-10% comparable EPS growth.
Cash generation and shareholder return discipline: FY2026 guided free cash flow of ~$12.4B and a 2026 dividend of $2.12 per share, the 64th consecutive annual increase.
Pricing power is the natural inflation hedge a long-term portfolio wants; concentrate pricing passes input costs to bottlers rather than absorbing them.
risks: PRICE. This is the single biggest risk in owning KO today. At $88.01 it trades at 26.4x TTM GAAP EPS and a 3.0% FCF yield for a business whose underlying unit case volume grew only 0.3% in 2025 (33.8B vs 33.7B cases). We are paying a growth multiple for a slow-volume business.

IRS transfer-pricing litigation. The Tax Court sided predominantly with the IRS on the 2007-2009 years ($3.3B of tax plus interest, of which KO already paid $6.0B in 2024 in response to IRS invoices). KO appealed to the 11th Circuit, which heard oral argument on 2026-06-25; a ruling could land any time. KO's own 10-K estimates the potential aggregate REMAINING incremental tax and interest for 2010-2025 at approximately $14 billion as of 2025-12-31 (~$3.25 per share) and says continued application of the Tax Court methodology would raise the effective tax rate by about 3.5 percentage points per year going forward. This is a live, near-binary event.

Leverage is not trivial for a staples name: gross debt $43.543B at 2026-07-03 against $16.371B of cash and securities, net debt/TTM EBITDA of 1.71x (2.00x at FY2025 year-end). Comfortable, but it removes balance-sheet optionality if the IRS case goes badly.

High payout. FY2025 dividends of $8.779B consumed ~77% of the $11.4B ex-fairlife free cash flow; buybacks were only $746M gross. Little cash is left to reinvest or absorb a shock, and the 64-year dividend streak makes cutting it practically unthinkable, which makes it a rigid claim on cash.

Earnings quality gap: FY2025 net income was $13.107B but GAAP operating cash flow was $7.408B, and even normalised FCF (~$11.4B) runs below net income partly because equity income from bottlers ($1.038B of 2025 equity income was not received as dividends) is real accounting profit that does not arrive as cash.

Currency. KO earns most of its money outside the US; FY2025 EPS carried an 8-point currency headwind and FY2026 guidance assumes a ~3% currency TAILWIND. A dollar reversal would flip a tailwind into a headwind and flatter-looking growth would evaporate.

Secular and regulatory pressure on sugary drinks: sugar taxes, health regulation, GLP-1 weight-loss drugs reducing consumption occasions, and packaging/plastics litigation (a Baltimore environmental suit is disclosed in the FY2025 10-K). Sparkling soft drinks are still 69% of volume.
Leadership transition risk: Henrique Braun became CEO on 2026-03-31 after James Quincey's long tenure. Execution under a new CEO is unproven over a full cycle.

Portfolio reshaping risk: the pending Coca-Cola Beverages Africa sale ($5.342B of assets held for sale) creates a 2-3% acquisitions/divestitures revenue headwind in FY2026 and makes reported comparisons noisy.
what_would_break_thesis: Consolidated gross margin falls below 55% for two consecutive quarters (FY2025 was 61.6%, TTM 61.9%).
Global unit case volume declines year-over-year for two consecutive quarters, signalling the brand is losing occasions rather than just trading price for volume.
Organic revenue growth (KO's own non-GAAP measure) falls below 2% for two consecutive quarters, or reported net revenue shrinks year-over-year for two consecutive fiscal years.
Net debt / EBITDA rises above 3.0x on a trailing basis (1.71x at 2026-07-03), or gross debt rises materially to fund the dividend.

KO loses the 11th Circuit appeal AND the ruling is applied to the 2010+ years, crystallising an obligation near the ~$14B the company itself has disclosed, or the ongoing effective tax rate rises by 3 percentage points or more on a sustained basis without an offsetting operational improvement.
The dividend is cut, frozen for a full year (ending the 64-year streak), or dividends paid exceed free cash flow excluding one-off items for two consecutive years.
Free cash flow excluding identified one-off payments falls below $9B in a full fiscal year (FY2025 normalised was $11.4B; FY2026 guided ~$12.4B).
Any serious accounting red flag, restatement, or auditor change.
Operating margin (comparable) falls below 28% for two consecutive quarters (Q2 2026 comparable was 35.6%).
catalysts: 11th Circuit ruling on the IRS transfer-pricing appeal (argued 2026-06-25). A win removes a ~$14B disclosed overhang and would likely re-rate the stock; a loss is the main downside catalyst.
Q3 2026 earnings, expected late October 2026, which will show whether the Q2 volume acceleration (+5% unit cases) is durable or a FIFA World Cup marketing effect.
Completion of the Coca-Cola Beverages Africa sale, guided to close in H2 2026, which would simplify the portfolio and return KO closer to a pure concentrate model.
A price pullback toward the $65-$70 zone, which would put the stock inside our fair-value band with the ~12% margin of safety our config requires (buy trigger roughly $67.50 or below).
A dollar rally that turns the assumed FY2026 currency tailwind into a headwind would likely create the cheaper entry price we want.
